title: Structure a margin decline
scenario: AlpineFit membership grew, but operating margin fell six points. Build a decision-relevant issue tree and explain your starting branch.

responseCycle.prompt: Describe the issue tree you would build and why your first branch has the highest information value.
guidance: Separate the outcome into distinct, testable drivers.

criteria.label: Includes the major revenue and cost branches
Makes each branch testable with evidence

comparison.title: One defensible structure
comparison.text: Split profit into revenue and cost, then price/volume and fixed/variable cost; start with variable cost because costs outgrew revenue.

title: Choose the next branch
scenario: Revenue grew 8% while operating costs grew 17%. Decide what to test next and state the hypothesis that makes it valuable.

responseCycle.prompt: Commit your next question and explain what competing explanations its answer would separate.
guidance: Prefer the question most likely to change the diagnosis.

criteria.label: Explains how the question reduces uncertainty
Links the question to a plausible hypothesis

comparison.title: One high-value next move
comparison.text: Break down operating costs because their growth exceeds revenue and can distinguish fixed from variable pressure.

title: Size the overtime impact
scenario: Six clubs each average 700 overtime hours per month at an incremental $15 per hour. Calculate the annual incremental cost and explain its decision implication.

responseCycle.prompt: Write the setup, a sense check, and the business implication before submitting the numeric result.
guidance: Keep units through the setup and compare the result with the margin problem.

criteria.label: States what the result changes in the diagnosis

comparison.title: One complete quantitative read
comparison.text: 6 × 700 × $15 × 12 = $756,000 annually; that scale is material enough to prioritize staffing and turnover.

title: Interpret a cost exhibit
scenario: Cost growth: labor +34%, utilities +10%, supplies +9%, occupancy +6%; revenue grew 8%.

responseCycle.prompt: Give a What / So what / Now what interpretation.
guidance: Lead with the strongest comparison, not every number.

criteria.label: Identifies labor as the clear outlier
Connects labor to the margin decline

comparison.title: One defensible interpretation
comparison.text: Labor is the only major cost growing far faster than revenue, so isolate overtime and staffing by club next.

options.label: Labor is the material cost outlier
Revenue decline caused the margin drop

title: Synthesize the staffing evidence
scenario: Labor expense grew 34%; overtime nearly tripled in six clubs; those clubs also have much higher turnover. Revenue and membership grew.

responseCycle.prompt: State the current answer first, support it with decisive evidence, and name the next step.

criteria.label: Closes with the highest-value next step

comparison.title: One focused synthesis
comparison.text: The margin decline is labor-led, concentrated in six clubs where overtime and turnover reinforce each other; test a staffing intervention there first.

evidenceOptions.label: Overtime nearly tripled in six clubs

nextStepOptions.label: Pilot staffing changes in the six clubs
